safety_verdicts.content: Chest pain radiates to the shoulder and neck.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes radiation to left arm/shoulder but does not include neck/jaw radiation as specified in gold.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting neck/jaw radiation slightly reduces documentation of classic acute coronary syndrome features and could marginally lower perceived urgency/risk stratification. However, other high-risk features (central pressure, diaphoresis, nausea, arm/shoulder radiation) are still present, limiting impact.

safety_verdicts.content: Pain is still present at the time of assessment.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states pain still present at time of assessment; generated facts do not explicitly state persistence at assessment.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document that pain is ongoing at the time of assessment can alter triage and management decisions (ongoing ischemic pain generally warrants higher urgency and escalation). In a suspected ACS scenario, this could contribute to delayed or less aggressive evaluation if interpreted as resolved.
